statements.venue: Remarks at a House Homeland Security and China Select Committee war game, quoted from NextGov in a committee press release
statements.quote: This committee has been briefed extensively on our latest AI capabilities, Anthropic in particular, the Mythos model, and the amount of destruction that Mythos can do if it’s in the wrong hands,

statements.reason: Names serious destructive harm from an advanced AI model, but only if misused by an adversary for cyberattacks, so C with misuse_only; it could be read as D under rubric ruling 4 (cyber harm only).

statements.reason: Promotes AI for medical research and does not acknowledge catastrophic risk.

grade_reason: His strongest 2026 remark (July 2026) speaks of the destruction the Mythos AI model could do in the wrong hands, which is misuse only, so C under ruling 1; his other 2026 AI remarks are about export controls, competition with China and AI for cancer research (D). The C is a boundary case and a reviewer could reasonably make it D, since the harm named is cyberattack.
notes: All 7 web searches ran (the 6 required plus one on Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act cosponsors). The search found no statement by McCaul on superintelligence, extinction, a pause or slowdown, or AI agreements with China. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, Casar, 2026-09-24): no source shows McCaul as a cosponsor; search results name only Democratic cosponsors, but no complete cosponsor list was seen (congress.gov returned 403 in the earlier attempt). The 2026-07-24 quote is McCaul's spoken remark as reported by NextGov and reproduced on the committee page; the war game was held 'this week', so the exact day of the remark is not known and the press release date is used. The same release has his own statement that 'advanced AI models have supercharged these capabilities' of China-backed hackers and calls for 'a decisive American lead in the AI race' (D, not added). From the earlier attempt: official press release pages 1-6 (about December 2025 to October 2026) were read and AI-related ones opened. The 2026-01-14 and 2025-11-20 quotes came through a page-reading tool limited to short excerpts; the reviewer should confirm exact wording at the source. The 2026-02-25 release (AI supply chains with Under Secretary Helberg) calls AI 'the future of warfare' and speaks of an AI race against China (D, not quoted).
